claims.text: Adding 1 at.% Al to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a protective aluminum oxide layer.
The aluminum oxide layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Adding 1 at.% Al will reduce the oxidation rate of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by 30% relative to untreated material during exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
The 1 at.% Al-modified alloy will retain at least 90% of the untreated alloy's room-temperature yield strength.
The 1 at.% Al-modified alloy will retain at least 90% of the untreated alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C.
The predicted oxidation protection applies at 800 °C in air for a 5-hour exposure without external loading.
The magnitude of the oxidation-rate reduction may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least 90% yield-strength retention, but the stated falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only below 80%. A result between 80% and 90% would violate the hypothesis while not falsifying it under the rule.

The predicted oxidation-rate reduction is 30%, whereas the experiment falsifies only reductions below 20%. Results from 20% to less than 30% would miss the quantitative prediction without triggering falsification.
